AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: primitive summoning protocols
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The first formal attempt to turn an abyssal response into a repeatable low-tier invocation procedure. It classifies small host calls as controlled contact rather than uncontrolled breach behavior.

unlocks.li: Gives the Protocol Matrix its first sigil layer.

notes.li: Preview entry only: current summoning unlocks remain controlled by existing systems.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: archon sigil handling
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: A sigil is not a trophy. It is a recorded permission event. This analysis teaches the colony how archon marks can be stored, read and reproduced without confusing them with normal resources.

unlocks.li: Prepares later boss sigil UI classification.

notes.li: No real boss gate is modified by this experimental matrix.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: elite summoning patterns
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The colony stops calling mass and begins calling function. Elite patterns describe specialized hostile formations: snipers, brutes, priests and support nodes.

notes.li: Intended to be linked to actual ritual defs only after the system is accepted.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: major boss invocation
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: A major boss invocation is not a stronger summon. It is a formal request for a domain-bearing authority to answer the colony directly.

unlocks.li: Frames domain boss access as protocol permission.

notes.li: Kept locked as a planned entry.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: crowned gate invocation
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The colony attempts to address an enemy infrastructure as an encounter. This is the invocation layer where the gate, anchors and waves become one hostile machine.

notes.li: Planned only. No current final gate logic is changed.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: infernal weapons
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The first abyssal weapons are not looted miracles. They are industrial translations of residue pressure into barrels, rails, conduits and lethal pattern logic.

requirements.li: Abyssal Forge or weapon fabrication loop available.

unlocks.li: Connects weapons to the Protocol Matrix.

notes.li: Current weapon recipes remain governed by existing forge progression.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: rift ballistics
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Rift weapons do not merely fire projectiles. They throw tiny shaped disagreements into local matter, forcing armor and tissue to resolve a hostile geometry.

unlocks.li: Explains rift carbines, needlers and lance behavior.

notes.li: Preview only; no stat changes are applied.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: heavy infernal systems
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Heavy infernal systems represent the point where the colony stops adapting guns and begins fielding mobile breach machinery.

unlocks.li: Classifies heavy weapons and anti-fortification systems.
Supports future gating for late weapons.

notes.li: Existing recipes are not blocked by this matrix.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: apex weaponry
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Apex weapons are not simply stronger. They are designed to be legally meaningful against entities whose bodies are only interfaces.

unlocks.li: Frames endgame weapons as anti-domain tools.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: anti-boss targeting doctrine
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Bosses require different target logic. This protocol defines the difference between killing a pawn and disrupting a domain-bearing battlefield function.

unlocks.li: Supports future tooltip and UI guidance for weapons.

notes.li: No targeting code is modified by this research UI.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: ashweave reinforcement
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Early protective systems teach the colony to survive contact residue without pretending it is normal armor material.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: abyssal armor systems
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Abyssal armor does not merely resist force. It teaches the wearer how to remain coherent while hostile breach pressure tries to rewrite the battlefield.

notes.li: No apparel defs are changed by this preview.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: gatebreaker carapace logic
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Gatebreaker doctrine treats armor as an answer to boss arenas, anchors and prolonged breach exposure rather than only bullets and claws.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: crownplate conditioning
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Crownplate systems must survive authority, not just impact. The plate is conditioned to resist orders written into matter.

unlocks.li: Frames crown-tier armor as domain resistance.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: dominion survival frames
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Dominion survival frames are built for maps that no longer behave like ordinary RimWorld spaces.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: basic implants
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The first implants move the Protocol from external infrastructure into colonist biology. This is power gained by making the body less exclusively human.

requirements.li: Basic implant workbench or forge loop.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: core integration
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: A core is not a battery. It is a functioning organ of the external system. Integration means the colony is no longer just studying debris.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: advanced implants
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Advanced implants treat the pawn as a compatible platform for alien command pressure, not merely a patient receiving surgery.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: rupture crown interface
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The Rupture Crown is not worn; it grants a position. Interface research documents the cost of making a colonist legible to crown authority.

unlocks.li: Frames crown artifacts and neural risks.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: gate anchor biology
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: A pawn can become more than a fighter. With sufficient loss of boundary, it can become infrastructure for the ritual itself.

unlocks.li: Classifies anchor implants and operator roles.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: circle safety interlocks
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Even a primitive circle requires ways to fail less catastrophically. Safety interlocks are not safety; they are survivable failure shaping.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: stabilized gate geometry
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The colony learns how to make a wound in the world open according to repeatable machine geometry rather than accident.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: containment logic
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Containment logic accepts that the door will misbehave. The task is to restrict how badly it is allowed to answer.

unlocks.li: Explains containment obelisks and mitigation systems.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: crown-tier conduits
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Crown-tier conduits carry authority, not just energy. They are designed for procedures where the breach must respect a higher access layer.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: final gate architecture
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The colony stops designing a circle and begins designing a battlefield-scale architecture of invasion, anchors and refusal.

unlocks.li: Frames final gate and anchor logic.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: residue processing
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Residue is not waste. It is matter that remembers being pressed by another law, and it can be compacted into the first useful abyssal reagent.

unlocks.li: Connects early economy to the Protocol Matrix.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: essence compression
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The colony standardizes hostile remains into a form the forge can reason about. This is where trophies become industrial feedstock.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: forge communion theory
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The forge is no longer a bench. It is a negotiated industrial interface where the colony learns to manufacture its future from enemy matter.

unlocks.li: Explains forge attunement and unlock language.
Supports future integration with Forge Console.

notes.li: No forge unlock rules are changed in this isolated version.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: crown logic decoding
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Crown shards are broken pieces of administration. Decoding them means reading authority as a protocol, not as symbolism.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: sanctified severance analysis
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Severance analysis studies how abyssal influence could be cut out of gear and replaced with cold controlled judgement.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: modular turret interface
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Abyssal turret modules are not just weapons bolted to steel. They are role-specific protocol organs fitted into a controlled chassis.

unlocks.li: Classifies turret modules as research family.

notes.li: Existing modular turret code remains authoritative.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: abyssal target acquisition
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Abyssal targeting does not ask only what is closest. It asks which hostile function must be interrupted before the breach escalates.

notes.li: No AI targeting logic is changed by this UI.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: breach lockdown systems
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Lockdown systems are built for enemies that should not be allowed to cross a line: elites, chargers and breach-born specialists.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: crownfire launch logic
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Crownfire launch logic turns artillery into ritual judgement: a long-range answer to entities that try to turn distance into authority.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: sepulcher rail calibration
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Sepulcher rails require calibration against targets that are less bodies than moving breach equations.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: heraldic fragment analysis
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Some fragments are not trophies. They are messages, addresses and permissions left by entities that speak from higher layers of the invasion.

unlocks.li: Frames Herald content as interpretation rather than loot.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: dominion protocol
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Dominion Protocol is the moment where the colony stops surviving answers and begins asking for administrative layers of the Abyss by name.

unlocks.li: Classifies dominion access as a right layer.
Supports final gate and post-game transitions.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: metadomain breach theory
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: The colony begins to suspect that known domains are only local interfaces, and that the true system is deeper than any boss can express.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: herald descent forecasting
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: Forecasting the Herald is not prediction. It is recognizing when a world has become legible enough to be announced.

AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.label: interface beyond the gate
AbyssalProtocol.ABY_ProtocolResearchDef.description: A final forbidden hypothesis: even godlike entities may be only the last readable interface of something that has no throne, no face and no ending.
